food.name: Hazelnuts
sourceNotes: Values are approximate representative placeholders for ruleset tuning, not a clinical nutrient database.

sections.title: Fats
sections.narration: 60.8 grams of fat. Saturated fat is 4.5 grams, which is reasonably controlled for a high-fat nut. Omega 3 is 90 milligrams, so it is not doing much for omega 3 support. Polyunsaturated fat is 7.9 grams, another weaker fat-quality mark. For nuts, the fat section matters because most of the calories are coming from fat.

sections.title: Carbs
sections.narration: 16.7 grams of carbs. Glycemic index is 15, helping the carbs behave steadily. Fibre is 9.7 grams, which is a useful fullness and digestion mark. Starch is 0 grams, so this is not really a steady-starch fuel. For nuts, carbs are not the main job, but fibre and sugar still decide whether the snack feels balanced.

sections.title: Proteins
sections.narration: 15 grams of protein. That amount is useful enough to count. Essential amino acids score is 5 out of 9, so the quality is okay but not strong enough to make this a main protein source. For nuts, protein helps, but it is still a supporting role.

sections.title: Vitamins
sections.narration: Vitamin E is 100% daily value, a huge strength for antioxidant support. For nuts, vitamin E can be the micronutrient that makes the high-fat package look much more useful.

sections.title: Minerals
sections.narration: Magnesium is 41% daily value, the best mineral here and useful for muscle, nerve, and energy-metabolism support. Iron is 26% daily value, a decent blood-and-oxygen mark. Zinc is 18% daily value, present but not strong enough to make immune support a headline. For nuts, minerals help justify the dense calorie package, and hazelnuts are good but not elite here.

sections.title: Pros
sections.narration: Positives first: still a recognisable whole-food option. That keeps them cleaner than most processed snacks. Holds up as a better snack default than most packaged options. That real-world swap value counts. Fat and texture help satiety. They can hold up better than many snack foods.
